title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 26
paragraphs: A few deserters had also come to them from Arcadia — men in need of livelihood, looking for employment. The Persians brought them into the king's presence and asked them what the Greeks were doing; one man put the question for all the rest. They said that the Greeks were keeping the Olympic festival and were watching a contest of athletics and horsemanship. The Persian then asked what prize they were competing for, and they told him of the wreath of olive that is given. At this Tigranes son of Artabanos uttered a very noble thought, though it brought upon him the king's reproach of cowardice: on hearing that the prize was a wreath and not money, he could not stay silent, but in the presence of everyone said: “Alas, Mardonius! What kind of men are these you have brought us to fight, who make their contest not for money but for honor!” So this was spoken by him.
